evidence.summary: With the other visible inputs held constant, increasing comorbidity_ratio from 0.009 to 0.5 reduced the score from 0.9797 to 0.9308.
Changing recent_admissions from 20 to 0 and 5.3 produced substantial score changes: 0.9780 at 20, 0.8753 at 0, and 0.9360 at 5.3.
With the other visible inputs held constant, requested_beds values of 1, 2, 0.3 and 0.2 produced different scores, with the score generally decreasing as requested_beds increased.
Changing ward from B to C while keeping the other visible inputs the same changed the score from 0.9787 to 0.9742.
Controlled age changes around the same baseline produced measurable score changes: age 75 produced 0.9794 while age 66.735 produced 0.9783 and age 72.735 produced 0.9821.
Changing baseline_score while keeping the remaining visible inputs constant produced small but measurable score differences across the tested values.
Changing prior_visits produced noticeable score changes in controlled observations, indicating that the feature contributes to the model output.

The observed DECLINE example has a score of 0.4287, while the tested APPROVE examples have substantially higher scores. This supports a strong relationship between score magnitude and the final decision, although the exact decision threshold was not established.
